Expectations for the hurried night
This section shows the plain rules
Companion Animal Travel Desk Operations

This section covers how the Companion Animal Travel Desk handles traveling pets from booking through handoff, so the desk stays calm, consistent, and safe. Staff should keep records current, check carrier fit and labeling, and make sure every pet has a clear care path before travel begins.

At intake, use the standard check-in packet and confirm the traveler details against the booking notes. <<FACT F086>> If anything is missing, stop the process and resolve it before the pet is accepted. Keep the language simple with the traveler, and never promise an exception that has not been cleared through the usual review.

During the booking review, check the animal's comfort needs, carrier condition, and any special handling notes. The desk should coordinate with ground staff so the pet moves through the journey without avoidable stress. If a traveler arrives with a worried pet, speak clearly, keep the area quiet, and make sure the handoff path stays orderly. When an issue needs formal reporting, <<FACT F108>> and record the facts plainly in the service log.

For arrival pickup, verify identity before release, then match the pet to the approved release details. <<FACT F101>> Do not release a pet to anyone who cannot be matched to the file, and do not rely on verbal claims alone. If the traveler is delayed, keep the pet in the approved care area and continue normal checks until pickup is complete.

Staff should keep notes factual, brief, and easy to follow. Avoid guesses, avoid emotional language, and pass along only what the next shift needs to continue the case. If a traveler gives new care instructions after booking, add them to the record and alert the right teammate right away. For anything unclear, contact the shift lead or the duty manager at once.
